To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the judiciary effectively came to make law in occupational accident cases; (ii) judges attempted to accommodate a new social and political reality to a legal framework that was increasingly out of touch with the new reality; (iii) judges articulated a particular solution to the ‘social question’; (iv) the judiciary's particular approach to the social question defined the kind of rights workers were able claim in court; and (v) this approach had a lasting impact on the development of the labour law
Argentine judges effectively came make labour law when they were ruling in occupational accident between 1900-1915.

1) Argentine judges effectively came, in the absence or inadequacy of a specific occupational accidents law, to make labour law by reinterpreting the Civil Code in occupational accident cases; 2) in doing so, Argentine judges attempted, in the context of an ongoing ‘social question’, to articulate a specific solution to the issue of workers' compensation;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the judiciary in the construction of the social question and the role of the social question in the construction of citizenship rights
how the Argentine judiciary came to define the rights and obligations of workers and employers in the early twentieth century.
the relationship between the judicial branch of government, the state and civil society, as it was played out in the courts of Argentina during this period.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
judges effectively made labour law when ruling on occupational accident cases between the years 1900 and the enactment of the first occupational accident law in Argentina in 1915.
the judiciary's solution to the social questions effectively defined the kind and scope of citizenship rights workers could claim in court.
the judiciary, by making labour law, was able to define the limits of citizenship rights for workers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in ruling in occupational accident lawsuits, Argentine judges articulated their own version of the ‘social question’ and, by doing so, effectively came to make the law of occupational accidents.
, in Argentina, judges effectively made law when ruling in cases of occupational accidents.

, by the end of the period, judges had effectively made a new kind of labour law that, although not necessarily in favour of workers, did recognize their right to compensation for occupational accidents and the right of the state to intervene in the labour market.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a context of legal uncertainty, judges are not mere interpreters of the law but, rather, are actively involved in shaping the legal system.
, in the absence or insufficiency of formal legislation, courts can be important actors in the making of social rights, including those related to labour.
, by looking at how judges dealt with specific cases, we can gain new insights about the role of the judiciary in the making of law.
